result: dlopen searches $ORIGIN elements of the program's and the caller's DT_RUNPATH/DT_RPATH and $ORIGIN names; RTLD_NOLOAD matches start-time objects by loaded name and ld.so by its PT_INTERP path
head: 8526d26e4

rulings.item: secure mode (AT_SECURE): dlopen applies to the program's $ORIGIN the same trusted-directory rule the start already uses; no set-uid probe possible without root

informational: brief item 1 premise no longer held: the start's and dlopen's search already followed the ld.so(8) order; only $ORIGIN elements failed under dlopen (program had no path in dlopen's loader; start-time objects lost their path)
$PLATFORM expands to haswell on x86-64-v3 (D-27.16); the reference gives x86_64 on the Zen 1 host: probe both CPU kinds in a loader story
start-time objects without DT_SONAME are still left out of a handle's local scope (adopt_deps matches soname or path only); given_name now has the name for a follow-up
dlopen through an LD_LIBRARY_PATH $ORIGIN list not probed on the reference; the test expects the start's rule
refused: Bash with a heredoc (python3 -I - handoff/DL-RUNPATH.md ... <<'X'), refused by the no-heredoc hook; my error, done with the Edit tool instead

impact.what: dlopen of a bare name / $ORIGIN name through a program's or library's $ORIGIN DT_RUNPATH/DT_RPATH now finds the library (was: not found)
dlopen(RTLD_NOLOAD) of a start-time library without DT_SONAME by its DT_NEEDED name, and of ld.so by its PT_INTERP path, returns the handle (was NULL)
RTLD_DI_SERINFO lists a $ORIGIN program's expanded entries (were missing)

improvement: sync_role reports BUSY while a plants job only reads the role to copy it; letting a sync through once the plants copy check has printed would save a wait
next_step: land; then the secure-mode ruling and the $PLATFORM probe on an x86-64-v3 Intel and an AMD host
